html:
SMTO-SCH-0016 — This prompt already has a running or paused schedule

GUID: 48cc4cba-a325-4005-82f2-0ad6fab19ac4
Slug: schedule-duplicate
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • SMTO allows only one running or paused schedule per prompt, and another one for this same prompt already exists. Your change was not saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the Schedules page and use the search to find schedules with the same prompt text. One of them is already running or paused, which is why this change was blocked.
  2. Select Edit on the existing schedule and put your new timing or wording there. Keeping one schedule per prompt stops the same work from running twice.
  3. If you really want this one instead, open the ⋯ menu on the other schedule, select Cancel schedule, then make your change here again. Once the other schedule is no longer running or paused, this one is allowed to take its place.

What success looks like

  • Only one schedule for this prompt shows as running or paused on the Schedules page, with the timing you want.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with the prompt's name. Don't delete schedules you haven't checked; they may belong to someone else's work.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Saving the schedule hit the unique index on live prompt schedules: another active or paused schedule already exists for the same prompt.

What this means

  • Schedule update catches a storage integrity constraint and reports the existing active/paused prompt-schedule conflict. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Schedule update catches a storage integrity constraint and reports the existing active/paused prompt-schedule conflict.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the existing prompt schedule and underlying safe constraint; this broad catch does not prove every integrity failure is duplication.

How to fix it

  • The update violated idx_agent_events_live_prompt (unique source_prompt_key where status is active or paused) and was rolled back. List schedules for the same prompt, then edit the existing one, or pause/cancel it before re-enabling this one; do not resubmit with a stale schedule ID.
  • Inspect existing prompt schedules and the safe storage constraint before deliberately editing the original or choosing a valid new schedule.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual constraint is resolved and only the intended active schedule is retained.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
